epicurves

Likelihood inference for epidemic curves. The package accompanies two manuscripts in preparation derived from Jaciele Oliveira’s doctoral thesis (Programa de Pós-Graduação em Estatística, UFPE). The scripts and results behind the numbers, tables and figures of the manuscripts are in analysis/.

  • Stochastic compartmental models under the Gaussian approximation. Any mass-action model is declared by its events (ga_model(), ga_event()), observed through the incidence of events or the prevalence of compartments, with under-reporting and time-varying rates, and fitted by maximum likelihood with a Kalman filter (ga_fit(), ga_profile(), ga_bootstrap()). The SIRD model fitted to daily cases and deaths has a dedicated interface (sird_ga_fit_inc(), sird_ga_fit_tv()).
  • Growth-curve ensembles on daily counts. Logistic, Gompertz and Richards curves are fitted by Poisson or negative binomial likelihood and combined with Akaike weights (fit_ensemble_incidence()); a series is divided into phases by penalised likelihood (bic_segment()) or by anytime-valid sequential e-detectors (edetect_segment()).

The paraiba_covid19 dataset holds the COVID-19 surveillance series for Paraíba, Brazil, used in both applications.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("Raydonal/epicurves")

# optional, needed by edetect_segment():
remotes::install_github("castlaboratory/edetect")

Example

Declare a SIRD model, simulate reported cases and deaths, and fit it:

library(epicurves)

sird <- ga_model(c("S", "I", "R", "D"), list(
  infection = ga_event("S", "I", rate = "lambda", by = "I"),
  recovery  = ga_event("I", "R", rate = "gamma"),
  death     = ga_event("I", "D", rate = "alpha")))
obs <- list(cases  = ga_incidence("infection", prob = "p", noise = "tau2"),
            deaths = ga_incidence("death", prob = 1, noise = "tau2_d"))

truth <- list(lambda = 0.6, gamma = 0.3, alpha = 0.1, p = 0.5, tau2 = 0.2, tau2_d = 0.1)
set.seed(1)
sim <- ga_simulate(sird, truth, c(S = 19990, I = 10, R = 0, D = 0), obs, n = 80)

init <- function(p) c(S = 1 - p$i0, I = p$i0, R = 0, D = 0)
fit <- ga_fit(sird, sim$data, obs, N = 20000, init = init,
              start = list(lambda = 0.5, gamma = 0.25, alpha = 0.15, i0 = 1e-3,
                           p = 0.6, tau2 = 0.3, tau2_d = 0.3))
confint(fit)

Divide the daily deaths in Paraíba into phases:

data(paraiba_covid19)
seg <- bic_segment(paraiba_covid19$new_deaths, d_min = 12, family = "negbin", step = 5)
paraiba_covid19$date[seg$cuts]

The articles on the package website work through both methods in detail. NEWS.md records the findings made while validating the package against the thesis.
